wrap verb

also wrap up, wrap a present, wrap in, wrapped, wrapping, swaddle

classical

Vulg. Lc. 2.7: pannīs eum involvit
Caes. BC 1.75: sinistrās sagīs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 409

involvō, involvere, involvī, involūtum

verb, third conjugation, transitive; what one wraps it in, ablative

wrap (in), wrap up

Wrap a present in paper, a baby in swaddling clothes, the left arm in a cloak. Of a person, sē litterīs involvere, to bury oneself in one’s books (Cicero, below). A wrapper is involūcrum (Traupman 409; see case).

Other words

  • obvolvō, obvolvere, obvolvī, obvolūtum — wrap round, muffle up

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 2.1.77; Cic. Verr. 2.5.72: capite obvolūtō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 409

    To cover all over, chiefly of muffling the head (capite obvolūtō) or bandaging a limb (Suet. Dom. 17).

Examples

  • et pannīs eum involvit, et reclīnāvit eum in praesēpiō

    and she wrapped him in swaddling clothes and laid him in a mangerVulg. Lc. 2.7

  • ubi salūtātiō dēflūxit, litterīs mē involvō, aut scrībō aut legō

    once the morning callers have drained away, I wrap myself up in books: I write or I readCic. Fam. 9.20.3

  • Dōnum chartā involvāmus.

    Let’s wrap the present in paper.composed

See also wrap up warm, gift, parcel, case, involve.
